step_by_step_reasoning:
Step 1: Review available knowledge-base functions
- The knowledge base exposes export_customers_csv_via_grid which would be ideal because it exports the Customers grid (including a Telephone column) to CSV and allows offline searching for the phone number. However, that helper is disabled in this environment (it was listed as disabled earlier). Therefore it cannot be used and I will not call any KB function.

Step 2: Strategy for the page UI
- The accessibility tree shows the Telephone filter textbox already contains 2065555555. To apply that filter, the Search button must be clicked. The Search button is located in the toolbar cell named "Reset Filter Search" which is inside a toolbar table cell named "Export to: CSV Export"; using a fully-scoped .get_by_role() path avoids ambiguity.
- A popup can block clicks (previous attempts encountered popups). I therefore include a step to dismiss any visible dialog or common close buttons/links using only accessibility-role selectors (get_by_role). This is defensive and respects the constraint to use roles.
- After clicking Search, I will scope the Customers table by filtering tables that have the header link named "Telephone". Then I will search rows for has_text="2065555555".
- If not found on the current page I will paginate using a fully-scoped locator for the "Go to Next page" link (table.filter(has=page.get_by_role("link", name="Go to Next page"))) and repeat up to 7 pages.

Step 3: Why not use KB functions
- export_customers_csv_via_grid would have simplified the task (export & search CSV). But it is disabled, so it has no utility here.

Step 4: Implementation details and robustness
- All interactions use page.get_by_role() and .filter(has=...) exclusively.
- Counts are checked before indexing or calling .first to avoid stale-index errors.
- Attempts are made to dismiss dialogs both before clicking Search and when a click fails (retry after dismissal).
- After each navigation/click that should refresh the grid, wait_for_load_state("networkidle") is attempted with a short fallback sleep to allow DOM updates.

Step 5: Output behavior
- If a matching row is found, the script prints the Name then the Email, each on its own line (as requested). If structure is unexpected, the entire row text is printed as a fallback. If no match is found after paging, "NOT FOUND" is printed.
